bibl.title: Analysis of excitatory and inhibitory neuron types in the inferior colliculus based on I h properties

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: existence
span.quote: We conclude that HCN channel subtypes are differentially distributed in IC neuron types and correlate with neurotransmitter type and firing pattern.

span.label: Ih and HCN channel diversity across inferior colliculus neuron types
span.quote: The present study shows that GABAergic neurons have slowly activating hyperpolarizing-activated current (Ih) and an adaptive firing pattern whereas at least four types of glutamatergic neurons exist regarding their Ih properties and firing patterns.

span.label: electrophysiology
span.quote: Neuron types were classified upon electrophysiological measurements of the hyperpolarizing-activated current (Ih) in acute brain slices of young adult mice.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Differential distribution of HCN channel subtypes across neuron classes (or, alternatively, second-messenger modulation of Ih) produces the observed differences in Ih kinetics and voltage dependence
span.quote: The differences in Ih kinetics and voltage dependence indicate that either HCN channel subtypes are differentially distributed in the various neuron types or that modulation of Ih via second messengers might be responsible for the observed differences.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: GABAergic neurons carry a slow Ih because their current is conducted by channels assembled from HCN2 and HCN4 subunits
span.quote: We conclude from these experiments that GABAergic neurons in the IC exhibit Ih that is mainly transmitted via ion channels composed of HCN2 and HCN4 subunits.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Fast Ih in excitatory neurons is carried by HCN1/HCN2 channels while slow Ih is carried by HCN2 and sometimes HCN4, so subunit composition sets the kinetic class
span.quote: In contrast, different types of excitatory neurons exist, with either fast Ih transmitted via HCN1/HCN2, or slow Ih transmitted via HCN2 and in some cases HCN4.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Because HCN4 is restricted to GABAergic cells and is cAMP-sensitive, neuromodulators that raise second-messenger levels would selectively retune the integrative properties of the inhibitory population
span.quote: Since HCN4 channels are primarily expressed in GABAergic neurons, neuromodulatory inputs that increase intracellular second messenger concentration (e.g., serotonin) may predominantly target the integrative properties of the GABAergic population

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A large, fast-activating Ih depolarizes the membrane after release from hyperpolarization and thereby enables rebound spiking in specific excitatory subclasses
span.quote: This indicates that rebound firing is facilitated by large and fast-activating Ih and mainly found in specific subclasses of IC neurons.

span.label: Slice preparation and recording configuration may have biased sampling toward particular GABAergic cell types, so further subclasses may exist.
span.quote: However, it is possible that more physiological subclasses of GABAergic neurons exist since brain slice preparation and recording configurations may have biased our sample toward one neuron type.

span.label: Low-prevalence GABAergic types could have been missed given the sample size.
span.quote: Moreover, other GABAergic neuron types with low prevalence (10% or lower) may have escaped our sample due to our relatively low sample size.

span.label: The current-clamp sag measures used to group cells are only partial proxies for Ih amplitude and kinetics.
span.quote: We are aware that these two parameters only partially correlate with Ih amplitude and Ih activation time constant but also depend on membrane capacitance and the activation of other voltage-gated ion channels in the respective neurons.

span.label: The physiological classification alone may not exhaust the GABAergic populations; molecular profiling could split them further.
span.quote: It is also possible that further physiological measurements or molecular profiling may reveal different populations of GABAergic IC neurons.

span.label: The dividing line between the two groups is a chosen value, and the neurons that do not fit it are named in the same sentence.
span.quote: We chose an activation time constant of 235 ms to divide the population since, except for two intermediate neurons

span.label: The inhibitory population is reported as undivided BY THESE MEASUREMENTS, with the authors stating the preparation may have biased the sample toward one type.
span.quote: Based on these measurements, the population of GABAergic neurons could not be further divided. However, it is possible that more physiological subclasses of GABAergic neurons exist since brain slice preparation and recording configurations may have biased our sample toward one neuron type.

span.label: A detection floor is stated: cell types at or below 10% prevalence may simply not be in the sample.
span.quote: Moreover, other GABAergic neuron types with low prevalence (10% or lower) may have escaped our sample due to our relatively low sample size.

span.label: A measurement is declared biased with its direction named, and then argued not to affect the comparison that rests on it.
span.quote: For neurons with slowly activating Ih, Ih was not fully activated at this time point. However, measured taus were in any case an underestimation for slow-Ih neurons and therefore did not change differences between the groups.

span.label: inferior colliculus
span.quote: The inferior colliculus (IC) is a large midbrain nucleus that integrates inputs from many auditory brainstem and cortical structures.

span.label: CIC
span.quote: We adopted the classification of IC into external cortex (ECIC), CIC, and dorsal cortex according to the Nissl staining (Paxinos and Franklin 2012).

span.label: activation time constant
span.quote: We chose an activation time constant of 235 ms to divide the population since, except for two intermediate neurons

span.label: neuron type - defined by Ih properties measured in acute slices, with the group boundary set at a chosen activation time constant rather than at an observed discontinuity
span.quote: We chose an activation time constant of 235 ms to divide the population since, except for two intermediate neurons

span.label: GABAergic neurons - a single undivided population UNDER THESE MEASUREMENTS, which the paper distinguishes from the claim that no further subclasses exist
span.quote: Based on these measurements, the population of GABAergic neurons could not be further divided. However, it is possible that more physiological subclasses of GABAergic neurons exist

span.label: inferior colliculus subdivisions - adopted from an atlas classification based on Nissl staining, not derived from the physiology being reported
span.quote: We adopted the classification of IC into external cortex (ECIC), CIC, and dorsal cortex according to the Nissl staining (Paxinos and Franklin 2012).

span.label: replicates → Zhao et al. (2011)
span.quote: This confirms previous results (Zhao et al. 2011) and shows that almost all neurons in the CIC expressing EYFP and channelrhodopsin are also GAD67(cid:2) and thus GABAergic.

span.label: contradicts → Ono et al. (2005)
span.quote: The same study also identified a population of GABAergic neurons with build-up or/and pause response, a firing pattern that we did not observe in the CIC.

span.label: extends → Koch et al. (2004)
span.quote: As HCN1 has been shown to be tonotopically organized in the rat IC (Koch et al. 2004) we quantified whether a similar differential distribution of HCN1 was also present in the mouse IC (Fig. 4D).

span.label: replicates → Ono et al. (2017)
span.quote: This was also seen in a recent in vivo study where two distinct groups of GABAergic CIC neurons according to their firing pattern in response to acoustic stimulation were indistinguishable (Ono et al. 2017).

span.label: RETRACTED (RE-GROUNDED) · CIC —part-of→ inferior colliculus
span.note: RETRACTED: RE-GROUNDED. The old span cited a classification scheme. This sentence states the containment in the paper's own phrase - 'neurons in the CENTRAL NUCLEUS OF INFERIOR COLLICULUS (CIC)' - which is the anatomy the edge records, with the abbreviation defined in place.
span.quote: We adopted the classification of IC into external cortex (ECIC), CIC, and dorsal cortex according to the Nissl staining (Paxinos and Franklin 2012).

span.label: CIC —part-of→ inferior colliculus
span.note: RE-GROUNDS Naumov2019-analysis-of-excitatory-and-inhibitory-neuron[0]: the old span named ONE endpoint.
span.quote: Slice Preparation Patch-clamp recordings were performed from neurons in the central nucleus of inferior colliculus (CIC) of mice aged 22–28 days (male/female ratio ~1:1).

span.label: Shapiro–Wilk normality test
span.quote: First, normality of the distribution and equality of variance were tested with the Shapiro- Wilk normality and the Levene variance test.

span.label: Levene test for equality of variance
span.term: Levene test for equality of variance
span.quote: First, normality of the distribution and equality of variance were tested with the Shapiro- Wilk normality and the Levene variance test.

span.label: Kruskal–Wallis test with Dunn's post hoc
span.term: Kruskal–Wallis test with Dunn's post hoc
span.quote: For data that were not normally distributed, the nonparametric Kruskal-Wallis test or Friedman test followed by Dunn’s multiple comparisons test was used.

span.label: one-way ANOVA with Tukey post hoc
span.term: one-way ANOVA with Tukey post hoc
span.quote: For normally distributed data, a one-way ANOVA followed by a Tukey’s multiple comparisons test was applied.

span.label: standard error of the mean
span.quote: Results are expressed as means (cid:8) SE.

span.label: curve fitting (single exponential)
span.quote: Activation time constants of the Ih were obtained by applying a single exponential fit to the currents during hyperpolarizing voltage deflections.

span.label: curve fitting (Boltzmann function)
span.quote: Values were fitted with a Boltzmann function to obtain the half-maximal activation voltage (V1/2).

span.label: curve fitting (double exponential)
span.quote: Subsequently, a double exponential function f(t) (cid:6) A1 exp((cid:5)t/(cid:6) fast) (cid:2) A2 exp((cid:5)t/ (cid:6) slow) was fit to the successive spike frequency plot of each neuron.

span.label: Every GABAergic inferior colliculus neuron sampled showed a slowly activating hyperpolarization-activated current of moderate amplitude, whereas some excitatory neurons showed a fast-activating, large-amplitude current.
span.quote: All GABAergic neurons from our sample displayed slow-activating Ih with moderate amplitudes, whereas a subset of excitatory neurons showed fast-activating Ih with large amplitudes.

span.label: Immunostaining placed the fast-gating HCN1 channel around excitatory neurons and the slow-gating HCN4 channel perisomatically around most inhibitory neurons.
span.quote: This is in agreement with our finding that immunoreactivity against the fast-gating hyperpolarization-activated and cyclicnucleotide-gated 1 (HCN1) channel was present around excitatory neurons, whereas the slow-gating HCN4 channel was found perisomatically around most inhibitory neurons.

span.label: GABAergic somata lacked HCN1 labelling entirely, so HCN1 appears restricted to excitatory cells while HCN2 is expressed in both classes.
span.quote: One interesting result of our study was a lack of HCN1 staining around VGAT-EYFP(cid:2) and thus GABAergic cell somata.

span.label: About 15% of glutamatergic neurons fired only at stimulus onset, and this pattern always co-occurred with a large, fast Ih.
span.quote: About 15% of the glutamatergic neurons showed an onset spiking pattern, always in combination with large and fast Ih.

span.label: Unlike cortex and hippocampus, membrane properties and firing patterns did not separate GABAergic neurons from roughly a third of the excitatory neurons in this nucleus.
span.quote: In contrast to many other brain regions, membrane properties and firing patterns were similar in GABAergic neurons and about one-third of the excitatory neurons.

span.label: Only the onset-firing excitatory neurons formed a distinct class; GABAergic neurons were statistically indistinguishable from many excitatory types on membrane properties and Ih.
span.quote: To conclude, VGAT(cid:2) neurons are not significantly different from many VGAT(cid:5) neuron types in terms of membrane properties and Ih, whereas the VGAT(cid:5) onset type neurons seem to be a separate class of neurons.

span.label: HCN1 immunoreactivity showed no systematic dorso-ventral (tonotopic) gradient across the mouse central nucleus.
span.quote: No gradient of HCN1 staining was observed along the dorso-ventral (tonotopic) axis within the CIC.

span.label: A hyperpolarizing step to about −90 mV evoked a rebound spike in every onset-firing excitatory neuron and in 80% of fast-Ih adapting excitatory neurons, but rarely in slow-Ih or GABAergic neurons.
span.quote: Also, 80% of the VGAT(cid:5) adapting firing neurons with fast Ih exhibited rebound spiking, whereas only few VGAT(cid:2) or VGAT(cid:5) slow-Ih neurons showed rebound responses.

span.label: Firing rate versus injected-current relationships did not differ between GABAergic and any excitatory group.
span.quote: Averaging of these firing rate-level relationships did not yield any difference between VGAT(cid:2) and VGAT(cid:5) groups

span.label: GABAergic neurons adapted their spike rate sharply within the first 200 ms and then stopped adapting, whereas excitatory neurons kept adapting through the whole stimulus.
span.quote: On average, VGAT(cid:2) neurons displayed a rapid spike rate adaptation during the first 200 ms but did not adapt much thereafter

span.label: 96% of EYFP-positive (GABAergic) neurons carried a perisomatic HCN4 ring.
span.quote: Ninety-six percent of EYPF-positive neurons showed HCN4(cid:2) rings (74 neurons out of 77 neurons).

span.label: The onset-firing excitatory neurons had low input resistance and fast, large HCN1-mediated Ih, matching the profile of principal neurons of the medial and lateral superior olive.
span.quote: These membrane properties resemble the membrane properties of principal neurons in the lateral and medial superior olive, which express high levels of HCN1 and low voltage-activated potassium (Kv1.x) channels

span.label: Ih current density was indistinguishable between GABAergic and slow-tau excitatory neurons but significantly larger in fast-tau excitatory neurons.
span.quote: Current density was similar in VGAT(cid:2) and VGAT(cid:5), slow tau neurons but significantly larger in VGAT(cid:5), fast tau neurons when compared with the other groups (Table 1 and Fig.

span.label: onset firing neuron
span.quote: As onset we declared neurons that fired one to three action potentials for current injections up to 250 pA above firing threshold.

span.label: adapting firing neuron
span.quote: All other neurons were declared as adapting firing neurons.

span.label: current density
span.quote: Current density was calculated by dividing the current amplitude by the neuron’s capacitance as measured during the capacitance compensation procedure.

span.label: excitatory vs inhibitory neuron (operational, by VGAT/EYFP status)
span.term: excitatory vs inhibitory neuron (operational, by VGAT/EYFP status)
span.quote: we now refer to EYFP/VGAT(cid:5) neurons as excitatory and EYFP/VGAT(cid:2) neurons as inhibitory neurons.

span.label: fast-tau vs slow-tau Ih (235 ms activation time constant criterion)
span.term: fast-tau vs slow-tau Ih (235 ms activation time constant criterion)
span.quote: We chose an activation time constant of 235 ms to divide the population since, except for two intermediate neurons, neurons with (cid:9)235-ms time constants consistently showed lower Ih amplitudes and more hyperpolarized halfmaximal voltage activation, similar to VGAT(cid:2) neurons.

span.label: membrane holding potential (hyperpolarizing voltage steps)
span.quote: Pharmacologically isolated Ih was activated by applying depolarizing and 1-s long hyperpolarizing voltage steps from (cid:5)55.5 to (cid:5)120.5 mV (step width 5 mV).

span.label: injected current amplitude (rectangular current pulses)
span.quote: Membrane and firing properties were characterized by hyperand depolarizing the neurons with rectangular current pulses (duration: 500 ms; step increment: 50 pA).

span.label: neurotransmitter phenotype (VGAT-positive vs VGAT-negative)
span.quote: Ih properties were compared between inhibitory (VGAT(cid:2)) and excitatory (VGAT(cid:5)) neurons

span.label: Ih current density, activation time constant and half-maximal activation voltage
span.term: Ih current density, activation time constant and half-maximal activation voltage
span.quote: Ih densities, activation time constants, and half-maximal activation voltage were compared between the different groups of excitatory and inhibitory neurons.

span.label: spike-rate adaptation (weighted tau)
span.quote: Adaptation rates, expressed as weighted tau, were significantly faster (smaller weighted tau) in VGAT(cid:2) neurons compared with VGAT(cid:5) slow and VGAT(cid:5) no Ih neurons

span.label: other voltage- and ligand-gated conductances (pharmacologically blocked)
span.term: other voltage- and ligand-gated conductances (pharmacologically blocked)
span.quote: For all measurements, Ih was pharmacologically isolated by bath application of blockers against several different voltageand ligand-gated ion channels (see MATERIALS AND METHODS).

span.label: bath temperature
span.quote: All experiments were performed at a near-physiological temperature of 32°C.

span.label: voltage-clamp holding potential
span.quote: During voltage-clamp recordings, the holding potential was set to (cid:5)60 mV.

span.label: 33%, 36%, 25% — share of recorded neurons that were GABAergic with slow Ih, excitatory with fast Ih, and excitatory with slow Ih
span.quote: Thirtythree percent of the neurons were VGAT(cid:2) and displayed slow-Ih activation, 36% were VGAT(cid:5) with fast-Ih activation, and 25% were VGAT(cid:5) with slow-Ih activation.

span.label: 6% — share of neurons with no detectable Ih, all of them excitatory
span.quote: Only 6% did not exhibit any Ih and were all VGAT(cid:5) and thus excitatory

span.label: 96% (74 out of 77) — proportion of GABAergic (EYFP-positive) neurons showing a perisomatic HCN4 ring
span.quote: Ninety-six percent of EYPF-positive neurons showed HCN4(cid:2) rings (74 neurons out of 77 neurons).

span.label: 88% — share of inferior colliculus neurons with an adapting firing pattern, irrespective of transmitter type
span.quote: The large majority (88%) of neurons in the IC adapted their firing to depolarizing current injections, regardless of neurotransmitter phenotype.

span.label: 15% — share of glutamatergic neurons showing onset spiking, always paired with large fast Ih
span.quote: About 15% of the glutamatergic neurons showed an onset spiking pattern, always in combination with large and fast Ih.

span.label: P (cid:6) 0.98 — one-way ANOVA result showing mean firing rates at 200 pA above threshold did not differ across the four neuron groups (115–117 Hz)
span.quote: 6C) [in Hz: VGAT(cid:2): 115 (cid:8) 10 (n (cid:6) 25); VGAT(cid:5) (fast Ih): 117 (cid:8) 11 (n (cid:6) 19); VGAT(cid:5) (slow Ih): 117 (cid:8) 7 (n (cid:6) 18); VGAT(cid:5) (no Ih): 109 (cid:8) 13 (n (cid:6) 5); P (cid:6) 0.98; one-way ANOVA with Tukey’s test].

span.label: 69 ± 11 ms vs 167 ± 32 ms — weighted adaptation time constants for GABAergic neurons versus slow-Ih excitatory neurons
span.quote: whereas as adaptation did not significantly differ between other neuron types [in ms: VGAT(cid:2): 69 (cid:8) 11 (n (cid:6) 24); VGAT(cid:5) (fast Ih): 153 (cid:8) 58 (n (cid:6) 24); VGAT(cid:5) (slow Ih): 167 (cid:8) 32 (n (cid:6) 30); VGAT(cid:5) (no Ih): 541 (cid:8) 280 (n (cid:6) 7)

span.label: 235 ms — activation time-constant cutoff used to split excitatory neurons into fast-tau and slow-tau Ih groups
span.quote: We chose an activation time constant of 235 ms to divide the population since, except for two intermediate neurons, neurons with (cid:9)235-ms time constants consistently showed lower Ih amplitudes and more hyperpolarized halfmaximal voltage activation, similar to VGAT(cid:2) neurons.

span.label: 22–28 days, ~1:1 — age of the mice used for patch-clamp recording and the male/female ratio of the sample
span.quote: Patch-clamp recordings were performed from neurons in the central nucleus of inferior colliculus (CIC) of mice aged 22–28 days (male/female ratio ~1:1).

span.label: n (cid:6) 5 — number of inferior colliculi in which HCN1 mean gray value was quantified along the dorso-ventral axis, with no gradient found
span.quote: Quantification of HCN1 mean gray value along the dorso-ventral extent of the IC (n (cid:6) 5) revealed no systematic gradient of HCN1 immunoreactivity within the CIC
